inline.s: (From the Dream Journey Collection: Instruction for Ou Jiake)

[A saying goes: 'Everyone eats and drinks, but few truly know the taste.' This speaks of the Way: it lies in the nearest everyday activities, yet few know it. The ancients said: 'Apart from dressing and eating, there is nothing else.' Thus, between ancient and modern times, those who are deceived by dressing and eating are many. If one is not deceived by them, one may be called a hero.]

The Doctrine of the Mean says: 'People eat and drink every day, but few are truly tasting the flavor (the great majority eat and drink while indulging in deluded thoughts).' This means that in the most ordinary activities of daily life, few people are able to remain constantly aware of what they are doing. Speaking of cultivating the Way, the ancient worthies said: 'Apart from dressing and eating each day, there is nothing else.' This shows that from ancient times to the present, those who are deceived by such daily activities as dressing and eating are very many. If one is not deceived by them, one may be called a hero.
[Dressing and eating] Here 'dressing and eating' refers broadly to all daily activities. [Apart from dressing and eating, there is nothing else]

(The Continued Transmission of the Lamp) [Not being deceived by them] In all the situations of daily life, to be clearly aware at every moment of what one is doing and what one is thinking.

[A student of the Way need not seek anything mysterious outside. If in all the situations of daily life one is not deceived by them, and sees through them at a glance right where one dresses and eats, this is the true upward effort. Those who aspire to the Way should practice in the midst of daily life.]

A student of the Way need not seek anything mysterious outside. If in all the situations of daily life one is not deceived by them, and sees through them at a glance right where one dresses and eats, and is not entangled by deluded thoughts, this is the true upward effort. Those who aspire to the Way should practice in the midst of daily life (cultivate the Way right in everyday living — maintaining mindfulness in every action).
[Upward effort] The effort of the upward road that transcends the sacred and the ordinary and goes beyond birth and death.

There is a Chan koan: one day Layman Pang was sitting alone in his hut when he suddenly said: 'Hard! Hard! Spreading ten bushels of sesame on a tree!' His wife, Mother Pang, then said: 'Easy! Easy! The meaning of the westward journey is on the tip of every blade of grass (the Way is everywhere — what is so hard about it)!' And his daughter Lingzhao said: 'Neither hard nor easy — when hungry, eat; when sleepy, sleep.' (These three were discussing the matter of cultivating the Way.)
[Dan (
dàn

)] A Chinese unit of capacity, ten dou making one dan. [Sesame] Sesame seed. [The meaning of the westward journey on the tip of every blade of grass] The Way is present in all things. 'A hundred grasses' is a metaphor for all things; 'the meaning of the westward journey' is the Way transmitted by Bodhidharma when he came from the West. [When hungry, eat; when sleepy, sleep] In daily activities, to be clearly aware at every moment of what one is doing and thinking, and not be deceived by them — this is cultivating the Way.
